text:
Priya: Heads up team 1010 10 I'm flying into Athens for the offsite next week. Two quick Qs: 1) arriving late night 1111 11 should I book the train or a taxi to the hotel? 2) adapters: Greece uses type C/F; should I bring a UK adapter too? Also weather looks iffy 327326, umbrella or rain shell?

Ethan: If you're arriving after midnight, taxis are much easier and safer (especially with luggage). Trains stop running relatively early. :taxi:

Luca: For adapters 1010 you only need EU (type C). UK adapter not necessary unless you're carrying UK plugs. I usually bring a tiny 2-in-1 travel adapter with USB-A/C ports.

travbot: travel-checklist: passport, hotel confirmation, local cash (~2000 EUR), contactless card, phone + charger, EU adapter (C), photocopy of passport, allergy meds. Note: Greek trains run ~05:30-23:30 on most lines.

Ariel: Umbrella if you don't mind extra bulk; packable rain shell is lighter and doubles as windbreaker. Also: request an early check-in if you're tired 62A.

Priya: Good point on taxis. Price estimate anyone? Trying to avoid a surprise 50EUR ride.

Jo: From Eleftherios Venizelos to central Syntagma area is usually 35-45 EUR in evening traffic. Agree trains won't help if you have heavy bags.

Ethan: Tip: request the official taxi queue at arrivals, not the random drivers. Also take a photo of the license plate and driver name into the group chat. Safety first.

Luca: Packing hack: put chargers/meds/one change of clothes in carry-on just in case checked bag is delayed at an international offsite. Also ziplock for liquids and a tiny tube of sunscreen (Athens sun is sneaky).

Priya: Small poll: react with :taxi: if you think taxi > train for late arrival, :train: if train is fine, or reply "depends". Also vote for umbrella vs shell: reply "umbrella" or "shell". I'll book based on the outcome.

travbot: Reminder: if booking taxis with the airport app, ensure driver is registered. Also check local SIM or roaming options if you need map access.
